newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Lung seeking to boost land bank.
newsitem.headline: Hang Lung seeking to boost land bank.

text.p: Hang Lung Development Co Ltd will aggressively increase its land bank in the current fiscal year through tenders or land auctions, chairman Ronnie Chan said after the group's general meeting on Tuesday.
"We will continue our aggressive effort in increasing land banks through different means such as tenders, land auctions or joint venture developments," Chan said.
"We will aggressively participate in bidding for land within reasonable prices."
Chan said Hang Lung has a land bank of about 11 million square feet, while its subsidiary Amoy Properties Ltd has a land bank of about seven million square feet.
"The existing land bank (of Hang Lung) can secure our development needs up to 1999," Chan said.
Hang Lung said in its latest annual report that there were several sizeable plots, some associated with the Mass Transit Railway Corp, for sale in the next few months.
"We hope to be successful in bidding for some of them," the report said.
Chan said he did not rule out the possibility of fundraising activities such as share placements or warrant issues if the price was right and the market tone good.
"The funds can be reserved for use in future land purchases," he said.

Commenting on the Sino-British Land Commission's move to double the amount of crown land disposable in the current fiscal year ending March 31, Chan said: "We welcome the move, it can slow the price rise of luxury apartments and that can enable Hong Kong to continue having a competitive edge (in the international market)."
The Hong Kong government said on Monday that China and Britain agreed 157.16 hectares of crown land would be disposed of this year in addition to the 153 hectares agreed in May.
